papers.title: Naturallyoccurring phytosterols in lipid nanoparticles induce rigidity reshape and endosome retention to enhance intracellular mRNA processing.
papers.abstract: Although lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have been widely used for mRNA delivery, understanding how cholesterol analogues modulate LNP properties and intracellular trafficking to enhance transfection efficiency remains essential for the rational design of next-generation delivery systems. This study investigated their structure-activity relationships and effects on mRNA delivery. We hypothesized that C-24 alkyl-substituted phytosterols enhance transfection by modulating LNP physicochemical properties and interactions with intracellular transport proteins. These phytosterols altered LNP mechanics an
papers.summary: This study shows that replacing cholesterol in mRNA lipid nanoparticles with naturally occurring phytosterols bearing C-24 alkyl substitutions changes the particles' mechanical rigidity and causes them to be retained longer in endosomes, which paradoxically improves intracellular mRNA processing and transfection efficiency. The work maps structure-activity relationships between sterol chemistry and LNP performance, offering design rules for next-generation mRNA delivery systems.

papers.title: Cryo-EM reveals a transmembrane allosteric site and activation mechanism for the SERCA calcium pump.
papers.abstract: Impaired sarco-endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (SERCA) activity contributes to defective calcium handling and cellular dysfunction in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, yet the structural basis of small-molecule SERCA activation has remained unknown. SERCA is a ubiquitous P-type ATPase that restores cytosolic Ca2+ to the sarco-endoplasmic reticulum and is essential for cardiac Ca2+ cycling and cellular energy homeostasis. Here, we used cryogenic electron microscopy to define how two chemically distinct activators, CDN1163 and UM-52, enhance SERCA function. Structures at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å r
papers.summary: Using cryo-EM, the authors determined structures of the SERCA calcium pump bound to two chemically distinct small-molecule activators, CDN1163 and UM-52, at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å resolution. They identify a previously unknown transmembrane allosteric binding site and propose a mechanism by which these compounds enhance SERCA activity. This provides the first structural basis for pharmacological SERCA activation, relevant to cardiovascular and metabolic disease.

papers.title: [Engineering CaNAT for alkali tolerance to enable whole-cell catalysis of nonivamide synthesis via artificial intelligence].
papers.abstract: This study aims to improve the stability of N-acyltransferase (CaNAT), the key enzyme for nonivamide synthesis, under alkaline conditions, for enhancing nonivamide production as nonivamide exhibits higher solubility in alkaline environments and further decipher the stability improvement mechanism. First, the solubility of nonivamide in buffer solutions at different pH levels was determined. On the basis of the solubility results, the Acidophilic and Alkaliphilic Enzymes Predictive model (acidophilic and alkaliphilic enzymes predictive model, AAEPre) was first fine-tuned via MP-TRANS. This mode
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: The study engineers the enzyme CaNAT to be more stable under alkaline conditions, where the product nonivamide is more soluble, to improve whole-cell biocatalytic production. The authors fine-tuned an AI model (AAEPre) to predict alkali-tolerant enzyme variants and used it to guide engineering. This demonstrates an AI-assisted protein engineering approach for improving industrial biocatalysis.

papers.title: [Functional characterization of aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductases in Clostridium ljungdahlii].
papers.abstract: To elucidate the functional division of aldehyde: ferredoxin oxidoreductase (AOR) isozymes in the ethanol synthesis of Clostridium ljungdahlii, we employed the CRISPR-Cas9 technology to construct single knockout mutants of aor1, aor2, and aor3 as well as the aor1/aor2 double knockout mutant. The functions of each AOR were systematically elucidated through fermentation experiments with CO as the sole carbon source, combined with quantitative real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) transcriptional analysis and protein structure prediction. The results showed that the
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: The authors used CRISPR-Cas9 to create single and double knockout mutants of the three aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (AOR) isozymes in Clostridium ljungdahlii and characterized their roles in ethanol synthesis during CO-based fermentation. Combining fermentation experiments, qRT-PCR transcriptional analysis, and protein structure prediction, they dissected the functional division of labor among AOR1, AOR2, and AOR3.

papers.title: [Intelligent enzyme engineering paradigm evolution and future toolkits].
papers.abstract: Enzyme engineering is undergoing a profound paradigm shift from experience-driven approaches to a novel dual-driven framework integrating data and mechanism insights. Grounded in massive biological datasets, this paradigm deeply integrates computational biology, artificial intelligence (AI), and synthetic biology to establish an intelligent, end-to-end pipeline spanning discovery, design, and application. For enzyme mining, the synergistic application of sequence/structure-based evolutionary analysis, graph neural networks (GNNs), diffusion models, and ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) p
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This review describes how enzyme engineering is shifting from experience-driven methods to a dual-driven framework that combines large biological datasets with mechanistic insight, integrating computational biology, AI, and synthetic biology into an end-to-end pipeline from discovery to application. It highlights tools such as graph neural networks, diffusion models, and ancestral sequence reconstruction for enzyme mining and design.

papers.title: [Catalytic bottlenecks and engineering strategies of post-modification enzymes heterologously expressed in microbial cells for plant natural product biosynthesis].
papers.abstract: Plant natural products represent a rich reservoir of pharmaceuticals and high-value bioproducts. However, their microbial biosynthesis is frequently constrained by inefficient post-modification steps. Key plant-derived post-modification enzymes, including cytochrome P450 monooxygenases, UDP-glycosyltransferases, O-methyltransferases, and prenyltransferases, often exhibit poor expression stability and low catalytic efficiency in heterologous microbial hosts. These limitations are primarily attributed to the absence of suitable membrane environments, protein misfolding, inefficient electron tran
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This review examines why plant post-modification enzymes (cytochrome P450s, glycosyltransferases, methyltransferases, prenyltransferases) perform poorly when expressed in microbial hosts for plant natural product biosynthesis, citing missing membrane environments, protein misfolding, and inefficient electron transfer as key causes. It then surveys engineering strategies to overcome these catalytic bottlenecks.

papers.title: [Advances in the biomanufacturing of noncanonical amino acids].
papers.abstract: Noncanonical amino acids are essential molecular building blocks for expanding biochemical functionality and structural diversity, and have demonstrated broad application potential in areas such as innovative drug development, biomaterial construction and enzyme engineering. However, their conventional production has relied primarily on total chemical synthesis, which typically involves complex synthetic routes, limited stereoselectivity and serious environmental pollution, making it difficult to meet the demands of large-scale and sustainable manufacturing. Consequently, biomanufacturing has
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This review surveys advances in biomanufacturing of noncanonical amino acids, which are valuable building blocks for drug development, biomaterials, and enzyme engineering but are traditionally made by polluting, low-stereoselectivity chemical synthesis. It discusses how biological production routes could enable more sustainable, scalable manufacturing of these compounds.

papers.title: [Construction of a high-tolerance and high-yield nisin-producing Bacillus subtilis based on the evolution of tolerance elements].
papers.abstract: As a host that is generally recognized as safe (GRAS), Bacillus subtilis is considered an ideal chassis for the heterologous synthesis of the bacteriocin nisin. Nevertheless, nisin is a potent antimicrobial peptide, and its accumulation during heterologous synthesis exerts a strong inhibitory effect on the growth of the chassis, leading to "self-toxicity" and the stagnation of product synthesis. To address this issue, this study proposes a tolerance engineering strategy, overcoming this limitation through the rational design and modification of nisin transporters. Initially, we constructed the
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study engineers Bacillus subtilis to produce the antimicrobial peptide nisin without succumbing to self-toxicity, by rationally designing and modifying nisin transporter proteins to improve tolerance. The resulting strain achieves both higher tolerance and higher nisin yield, demonstrating a tolerance-engineering strategy for heterologous production of toxic antimicrobial peptides.

papers.title: [Advances in ProteinMPNN-driven protein engineering].
papers.abstract: Biomanufacturing is a key pathway for promoting the green transformation of conventional production methods. Its core bottleneck lies in the difficulty of natural enzymes to meet the requirements of industrial applications, necessitating the customized modification of enzyme molecules through protein engineering. Conventional semi-rational design is limited by a narrow sequence search space, heavy reliance on known structural information, and high experimental screening costs, which make it difficult to achieve precise design of industrial-grade enzyme molecules. In recent years, artificial in
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This review summarizes how ProteinMPNN, a deep-learning-based inverse protein folding model, is being applied to protein engineering for biomanufacturing. It contrasts conventional semi-rational design—limited by narrow sequence search space, dependence on known structures, and costly screening—with ProteinMPNN-driven approaches that enable more precise design of industrial-grade enzymes. The article surveys recent advances in using this tool to customize enzyme molecules for industrial applications.

papers.title: Biophysically grounded deep learning improves protein-protein ΔΔG prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of mutation-induced changes in protein-protein binding free energy (ΔΔG) remains limited by small, redundant datasets and train-test homology leakage. We show that commonly used SKEMPI2 splits inflate model performance, with every tested AI predictor declining under a stringent split that controls homology at the level of individual chains (60% sequence identity). We introduce ProtBFF, a modular framework that integrates five residue-level biophysical descriptors into pretrained protein representations through cross-embedding attention. Under leakage-controlled evaluation,
papers.summary: The paper shows that standard SKEMPI2 train-test splits overestimate the accuracy of AI models for predicting mutation-induced changes in protein-protein binding affinity (ΔΔG) due to homology leakage. The authors introduce ProtBFF, a modular framework that combines five residue-level biophysical descriptors with pretrained protein representations via cross-embedding attention, and demonstrate improved performance under a stringent homology-controlled split (60% sequence identity at the chain level).

papers.title: Advances in photothermal nanozymes: from rational design to multifunctional theranostic platforms.
papers.abstract: Photothermal nanozymes integrate enzyme-like catalysis with photothermal conversion, where localized hyperthermia accelerates kinetics, improves substrate accessibility, and modulates biological barriers to achieve synergistic amplification beyond monotherapies. This review systematically surveys design strategies and applications, with highlights centered on three interconnected aspects. A composition-based classification framework is first established, covering noble metals, transition metal compounds, carbon-based materials, Prussian blue analogues, single-atom catalysts, and metal-organic
papers.summary: This review surveys photothermal nanozymes, which combine enzyme-mimicking catalysis with light-driven heating to enhance reaction rates and substrate access. It proposes a composition-based classification (noble metals, transition metal compounds, carbon materials, Prussian blue analogues, single-atom catalysts, MOFs) and discusses design strategies and multifunctional theranostic applications. The focus is on how localized hyperthermia synergistically amplifies catalytic therapy beyond single-modality treatments.

papers.title: Reprogramming IL‑2 Receptor-Binding Selectivity: A Computational Strategy for Engineering Receptor-Binding Profiles.
papers.abstract: Interleukin-2 (IL-2) immunotherapy is limited by off-target toxicity and the unintended activation of immunosuppressive regulatory T cells (Tregs). Here, we present a free-energy-guided computational and experimental workflow for stepwise reprogramming of the IL-2 receptor-binding profile. We first used molecular dynamics simulations, alanine scanning, interaction entropy-corrected binding free energy analysis, combinatorial mutation design, and thermodynamic integration to identify mutations that enhance IL-2Rα binding. Among the IL-2Rα-directed variants, IM7 showed the strongest apparent enh
papers.summary: The authors developed a computational workflow combining molecular dynamics, alanine scanning, and free-energy calculations to rationally engineer IL-2 variants with altered receptor-binding selectivity. They identified mutations that enhance binding to the IL-2Rα subunit, with variant IM7 showing the strongest apparent improvement, aiming to reduce off-target toxicity and Treg activation in IL-2 immunotherapy.

papers.title: An Integrated Ligand- and Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Experimental Strategy for the Prediction of Chemically Diverse GLP-1R Agonists.
papers.abstract: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) plays a central role in metabolic regulation and is a major therapeutic target for obesity and diabetes. Peptide agonists, like semaglutide, targeting GLP-1R, remain among the most effective regulators of glucose metabolism and appetite. Nonetheless, recent reports of weight regain after treatment discontinuation sustain the interest in expanding the chemical diversity of GLP-1R ligands through drug discovery strategies. However, the structural complexity and conformational plasticity of class B1 G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) make conventiona
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper combines ligand-based and structure-based virtual screening with experimental validation to identify chemically diverse small-molecule agonists of GLP-1R, a key target for obesity and diabetes. The approach addresses the difficulty of targeting class B1 GPCRs, which are structurally complex and flexible, and aims to expand beyond peptide-based drugs like semaglutide.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for Aligning Structure-Based Molecular Generation toward Make-on-Demand Chemical Spaces.
papers.abstract: Generative models for structure-based drug design have strong potential to accelerate early-stage drug discovery by enabling the conditional generation of target-specific molecules. However, a major bottleneck is that generated compounds are frequently difficult or impossible to synthesize, limiting their direct experimental validation and utility. We address this by optimizing for membership in make-on-demand chemical libraries, ensuring that generated molecules can be directly purchased and tested. To this end, we apply reinforcement learning to a pocket-conditioned generative molecular mode
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors apply reinforcement learning to a pocket-conditioned generative molecular model to bias generated compounds toward molecules that are available in make-on-demand chemical libraries. This addresses the common bottleneck that structure-based generative models often produce molecules that are difficult or impossible to synthesize, limiting experimental validation. The approach aims to ensure generated candidates can be directly purchased and tested.

papers.title: AARS1-Mediated GLUD1 K503 Lactylation Drives Colorectal Cancer Metastasis Through Post-Transcriptional Reprogramming.
papers.abstract: The prognosis of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) largely depends on whether metastasis occurs. The Warburg effect leads to lactate accumulation and potential lysine lactylation (Kla), thereby promoting tumor initiation and progression. However, the role of non-histone Kla in CRC metastasis remains poorly understood. In this study, integrated lactylome and proteome profiling of liver metastases (LM) and paired primary tumors (PT) from patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), together with multi-omics analyses and in vitro and in vivo validation, identified GLUD1 as a key lactyla
papers.summary: This study integrates lactylome and proteome profiling of liver metastases versus paired primary tumors in metastatic colorectal cancer patients, identifying GLUD1 as a key lactylated protein. The authors show that AARS1 mediates lactylation of GLUD1 at lysine 503, which drives colorectal cancer metastasis through post-transcriptional reprogramming. The work links the Warburg effect's lactate accumulation to non-histone lysine lactylation as a driver of metastatic progression.

papers.title: Propolis, Quorum Sensing, and Biofilms in Canine Skin and Ear Infections: Evidence and Research Priorities.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Secondary bacterial and yeast infections contribute to antimicrobial use in dogs with atopic dermatitis. This review examines whether propolis modulates quorum sensing (QS) or biofilm-associated traits relevant to canine skin and ear infections. Methods: The narrative synthesis was informed by a structured PubMed search on 12 October 2026, sensitivity searches, and targeted retrieval. Results: Propolis preparations and constituents altered QS-associated phenotypes and biofilm endpoints, mostly in biosensors and non-canine models. Studies of canine isolates mainly measure
papers.summary: This narrative review examines whether propolis (a bee-derived resin) can interfere with quorum sensing and biofilm formation in bacteria and yeast that cause secondary skin and ear infections in dogs with atopic dermatitis. The authors found that propolis and its constituents alter QS-associated phenotypes and biofilm endpoints, but almost all evidence comes from biosensor strains and non-canine models, with canine-isolate studies limited in scope. They conclude by outlining research priorities needed to establish whether propolis is a viable antimicrobial-sparing strategy in veterinary dermatology.

papers.title: Antibacterial and Antifungal Activity of Anticancer-Active Diazaphenothiazine Derivatives: Experimental Evaluation and Molecular Docking Studies.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance necessitates the development of new agents with enhanced efficacy and well-characterized mechanisms of action. This issue is particularly relevant to bacterial and fungal superinfections associated with anticancer therapy. This study evaluated the antibacterial and antifungal activities (expressed as IC50) of two diazaphenothiazine derivatives with previously demonstrated anticancer properties: the parent compound, 10H-2,7-diazaphenothiazine (BM1), and its 10-(1-methyl-4-nitroimidazole) derivative (BM2). Methods: Antimicrob
papers.summary: This study tested two diazaphenothiazine derivatives (BM1 and BM2), previously shown to have anticancer activity, for antibacterial and antifungal effects, measuring IC50 values. Molecular docking was used to explore potential mechanisms of action. The work aims to identify compounds that could address bacterial and fungal superinfections during anticancer therapy.

papers.title: Phenotypic expansion of TUBGCP6 primary microcephaly: severe cortical malformations without chorioretinopathy and insights into variant interpretation.
papers.abstract: Biallelic variants of TUBGCP6 are associated with primary microcephaly, chorioretinopathy, short stature, and intellectual disability (ID). Most reported cases had at least one loss-of-function variant.
papers.summary: This paper reports new cases of TUBGCP6-related primary microcephaly, expanding the known phenotype to include severe cortical malformations without chorioretinopathy. It also provides insights into how to interpret TUBGCP6 variants, noting that most previously reported cases carried at least one loss-of-function variant.

papers.title: Predictive RNA-Ligand Binding Free Energy Perturbation through Preparatory Simulations and Polarizable Force Fields.
papers.abstract: Free energy perturbation (FEP) has become a cornerstone of structure-based drug design, yet its success has been built almost entirely on protein targets. Extending this physical rigor to RNA─an emerging and largely untapped therapeutic target class─confronts challenges that protein-ligand systems rarely impose: pronounced conformational flexibility, dense and highly anisotropic electrostatics, and ligand binding that frequently depends on direct metal coordination. Whether and when these challenges demand more sophisticated physical models has remained an open question. Here, we address it th
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: This paper extends free energy perturbation (FEP), a standard computational method for predicting protein-ligand binding affinities, to RNA-ligand systems, which pose unique challenges like high flexibility, anisotropic electrostatics, and metal-dependent binding. The authors show that preparatory simulations combined with polarizable force fields can make FEP predictive for RNA targets, addressing when more sophisticated physical models are needed. This work opens the door to rigorous structure-based drug design against RNA, an emerging therapeutic target class.

papers.title: Enhancing Enzyme pH Adaptation for Industrial Biocatalysis: From Sequence-Dependent Engineering to Sequence-Independent Stabilization.
papers.abstract: Enzymes are indispensable biocatalysts in industrial processes, but their application is often restricted by narrow pH optima. Exposure to acidic or alkaline conditions alters the protonation states of ionizable residues, disrupts catalytic microenvironments and stabilizing interactions, and ultimately reduces activity, catalytic efficiency, or structural integrity. This limitation is particularly important in industrial sectors such as detergents, textiles, biorefineries, and therapeutic formulations, where operation under non-native pH conditions is frequently required. Conventional sequence
papers.summary: This review examines how enzymes can be engineered to tolerate non-native pH conditions for industrial biocatalysis. It distinguishes sequence-dependent approaches, which modify ionizable residues to shift pH optima, from sequence-independent stabilization strategies that protect enzyme structure without altering the primary sequence. The authors frame these complementary routes as a practical roadmap for improving enzyme performance in detergents, textiles, biorefineries, and therapeutic formulations.

papers.title: Phytochemical Profiling and Biological Activities of Moroccan Juniperus phoenicea L. Leaf Extracts: UHPLC-MS Analysis, Molecular Docking, and ADMET Predictions.
papers.abstract: Juniperus phoenicea L. is a medicinal plant native to the Mediterranean region, including Morocco, where it is traditionally used to treat various ailments. This study aimed to characterize the phytochemical profiles of aqueous, ethanolic, and hydroethanolic leaf extracts of Moroccan J. phoenicea and evaluate their antioxidant, antibacterial, and antifungal activities. Potential interactions between the extracts and conventional antimicrobial agents were also investigated, alongside molecular docking analyses of selected phytochemicals and in silico predictions of their pharmacokinetic and tox
papers.summary: This study profiles the phytochemical composition of Moroccan Juniperus phoenicea leaf extracts using UHPLC-MS and evaluates their antioxidant, antibacterial, and antifungal activities, including potential synergy with conventional antimicrobial drugs. Molecular docking and ADMET predictions were used to explore how selected phytochemicals might interact with biological targets and their drug-likeness. The work is largely descriptive and in silico, characterizing a traditional medicinal plant's chemistry and bioactivity.

papers.title: Revealing the Mechanism of Porous Graphene in Styrene-Butadiene-Styrene/Crumb Rubber-Modified Asphalt: A Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: Clarifying the interaction between graphene and styrene-butadiene-styrene block copolymer (SBS)/crumb rubber (CR)-modified asphalt is essential for applying graphene-modified asphalt. Therefore, the mechanical properties of SBS/CR-modified asphalt incorporating different dosages of porous graphene (PG) were investigated via molecular dynamics simulation to elucidate PG's role and mechanism in the SBS/CR/asphalt blend system. The results demonstrate that high-temperature elasticity and low-temperature flexibility of SBS/CR-modified asphalt were most effectively improved at a PG content of 2%. C
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how porous graphene (PG) affects styrene-butadiene-styrene/crumb rubber-modified asphalt. The authors find that a 2% PG content most effectively improves the blend's high-temperature elasticity and low-temperature flexibility, and they propose a mechanism for PG's role in the system. The work is a computational materials study rather than a biological or biomedical one.

papers.title: Mechanistic Study of Xanthohumol Against Rheumatoid Arthritis via Regulation of p38/MAPK Pathway.
papers.abstract: To elucidate the molecular mechanism by which xanthohumol (XN) alleviates rheumatoid arthritis (RA), this study integrated network pharmacology prediction, proteomic screening, and molecular dynamics simulation to systematically evaluate the inhibitory effects and targets of XN in TNF-α-induced fibroblast-like synoviocytes (MH7A cells). XN dose-dependently reversed the pathological proliferation and invasive behavior of MH7A cells and down-regulated pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-1β and IL-6, as well as fibrosis/angiogenesis-related factors including TGF-β1 and VEGF. Cross-validation of
papers.summary: This study combines network pharmacology, proteomics, and molecular dynamics simulation to show that xanthohumol, a natural compound, reduces rheumatoid arthritis pathology in fibroblast-like synoviocytes by inhibiting the p38/MAPK pathway. XN dose-dependently reversed abnormal cell proliferation and invasion and lowered inflammatory and fibrosis/angiogenesis factors like IL-1β, IL-6, TGF-β1, and VEGF. The work provides mechanistic support for xanthohumol as a potential RA therapeutic.

papers.title: Metalloenzymes as Biosynthetic Hooks for RiPP Natural Product Discovery: Genome Mining, Catalytic Innovation, and Biological Function.
papers.abstract: Ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) constitute one of the most rapidly expanding classes of natural products, yet a substantial fraction of their biosynthetic diversity remains hidden within uncharacterized microbial genomes. Metal-dependent enzymes are increasingly emerging as powerful biosynthetic signatures because their cofactor requirements, sequence motifs, structural architectures, and genomic contexts can provide mechanistic clues to otherwise cryptic biochemical transformations. This review critically examines the use of metalloenzymes as biosynt
papers.summary: This review examines how metal-dependent enzymes can serve as biosynthetic signatures to guide genome mining for ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs), a rapidly expanding class of natural products whose diversity remains largely unexplored. The authors discuss how cofactor requirements, sequence motifs, structural features, and genomic contexts of metalloenzymes provide mechanistic clues to cryptic biosynthetic transformations, and they survey catalytic innovations and biological functions of these systems.

papers.title: In Silico and In Vitro Studies on Selective MAO-B Inhibition and Predicted Microbiome Interactions of Novel Chalcone Derivatives: Relevance to the Gut-Brain Axis in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) lacks pharmacological therapies for its core features. This study synthesized chalcone derivatives, determined their monoamine oxidase A (MAO-A) and MAO-B inhibitory profiles, and generated computational hypotheses regarding MAO-B binding, gut-bacterial protein interactions, and drug-like properties. Methods: Sixteen chalcones (23-38; fifteen newly reported) were synthesized and characterized. MAO-A and MAO-B inhibition was measured using fluorometric concentration-response assays, with clorgyline and safinamide as references. Compounds 23,
papers.summary: This study synthesized sixteen novel chalcone derivatives and tested their ability to selectively inhibit monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B) versus MAO-A, finding some compounds with promising selectivity. Computational docking predicted that these compounds may also interact with gut bacterial proteins, suggesting a possible role in modulating the gut-brain axis relevant to autism spectrum disorder. The work is preliminary, combining in vitro enzyme assays with in silico predictions, but does not yet demonstrate efficacy in ASD models.

papers.title: Exploiting the Class IIa-Specific Hydrophobic Pocket: A Linker-Driven Strategy for Designing HDAC7-Targeted Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Histone deacetylase 7 (HDAC7), a class IIa epigenetic regulator, is implicated in the progression of multiple malignancies; however, the development of selective HDAC7 inhibitors remains challenging due to the high structural conservation among HDAC isoforms, particularly with the closely related class IIb enzyme HDAC6. Methods: In this study, we screened a focused library of hydroxamate-based inhibitors to define the structural determinants governing HDAC7 isoform selectivity. While most compounds exhibited a strong preference for HDAC6, inhibitors bearing aromatic link
papers.summary: This study screened a focused library of hydroxamate-based inhibitors to identify structural features that drive selectivity for HDAC7 over the closely related HDAC6. Most compounds preferred HDAC6, but inhibitors with aromatic linkers could exploit a class IIa-specific hydrophobic pocket to achieve HDAC7 selectivity. The work provides a structure-based design strategy for developing more selective HDAC7 inhibitors.

papers.title: Antioxidants from Onion (Allium cepa L.): Current Evidence, Redox Mechanisms, and an AI-Assisted Discovery Framework.
papers.abstract: Allium cepa L. (onion) is a globally important vegetable crop and functional food recognized for its rich diversity of antioxidant phytochemicals, including flavonoids, organosulfur compounds, phenolic acids, anthocyanins, saponins, and polysaccharides. Onion-derived phytochemicals have demonstrated antioxidant and redox-modulating activities in chemical, cellular, and animal studies. However, onion-specific applications of artificial intelligence and structure-based computational methods remain limited. This review therefore discriminates established experimental evidence from computational p
papers.summary: This review surveys the antioxidant phytochemicals in onion (flavonoids, organosulfur compounds, phenolic acids, anthocyanins, saponins, and polysaccharides) and the redox mechanisms they modulate in chemical, cellular, and animal studies. It also proposes an AI-assisted, structure-based computational framework for discovering and prioritizing onion-derived antioxidant compounds, noting that such applications remain limited for this crop.

papers.title: Integrating artificial intelligence prescreening with molecular dynamics for the design of peptide-based WWP1 inhibitors as promising therapeutic agents against breast cancer, including the triple-negative subtype.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most frequently diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related death in women. BC is classified into three primary subtypes, of which triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) carries the poorest prognosis because it lacks specific targetable markers. Preclinical studies of TNBC have consistently reported reduced tumor-suppressor activity of PTEN, activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. Notably, published studies have shown that the WWP1 enzyme plays a pivotal role in driving PTEN degradation via ubiquitination, identifying it as a promising therap
papers.summary: This study uses AI-based prescreening combined with molecular dynamics simulations to design peptide inhibitors targeting the WWP1 enzyme, which drives degradation of the tumor suppressor PTEN in breast cancer. The work aims to develop therapeutic candidates particularly for triple-negative breast cancer, which lacks targeted treatment options. The approach integrates computational screening with simulation to identify and validate peptide-based inhibitors.

papers.title: Machine Learning and Structure-Based Virtual Screening for Reliability-Aware G Protein-Coupled Receptor Ligand Prioritization.
papers.abstract: Background: Predictive performance is necessary but insufficient for G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) ligand prioritization, where heterogeneous bioactivity data, analog-series overlap, receptor-state dependence, and polypharmacology can weaken high-scoring predictions. Methods: We developed an auditable ligand- and structure-based workflow across five human GPCRs: DRD2, CB2, ADORA2A, OPRM1, and CCR5. ChEMBL Ki, IC50, and EC50 data were evaluated using scaffold-disjoint validation, external validation, Venn-Abers calibration, conformal prediction, applicability-domain analysis, explainability
papers.summary: The authors present an auditable virtual screening workflow that combines ligand-based machine learning with structure-based docking across five human GPCRs (DRD2, CB2, ADORA2A, OPRM1, CCR5). They emphasize reliability-aware evaluation using scaffold-disjoint and external validation, Venn-Abers calibration, conformal prediction, applicability-domain analysis, and explainability, arguing that high predictive scores alone are insufficient for GPCR ligand prioritization. The work is a methodological contribution aimed at making computational hit prioritization more trustworthy.

papers.title: Minimal Mutagenesis Resurrects Human Uricase with Attenuated Immunogenicity.
papers.abstract: The human uricase (UOX) gene was pseudogenized during evolution, leaving uric acid as the terminal product of purine metabolism. Heterologous uricases can elicit anti-drug antibodies, which limit their long-term use. Here, we restored activity to a human-pseudogene-derived uricase reference through molecular-evolution-guided rational design. Sequence alignment guided the construction of reversion mutants by overlap-extension PCR and two rounds of combinatorial optimization. Structural modeling and an accelerated co-culture dendritic cell (acDC) assay were used to generate mechanistic hypothese
papers.summary: The authors resurrected the human uricase enzyme, which was pseudogenized during evolution, using molecular-evolution-guided rational design and minimal mutagenesis. They generated reversion mutants via overlap-extension PCR and two rounds of combinatorial optimization, and used structural modeling plus an accelerated dendritic cell co-culture assay to assess immunogenicity. The resulting enzyme shows restored activity with attenuated immunogenicity, potentially addressing the anti-drug antibody problem that limits heterologous uricase therapies.

papers.title: Computational and Experimental Studies of PSMA-Targeted Conjugates Designed for Subcellular Delivery of Theranostic Radiometals to Prostate Cancer Cells.
papers.abstract: Background: The membrane receptor prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a validated target for theranostic radioconjugates in the treatment and imaging of prostate cancer (PCa). Radioconjugates targeted at PSMA rely mostly on the peptidomimetic glutamate-urea-lysine (Glu-urea-Lys) binding motif to facilitate tumor accumulation. The combination of this binding motif with subcellular targeting moieties, such as acridine orange (AO) and triphenylphosphonium (TPP) derivatives, for nuclear and mitochondrial delivery, respectively, might open the way to innovative dual-target approaches. This
papers.summary: This study computationally designs and experimentally tests PSMA-targeted radioconjugates that combine the Glu-urea-Lys binding motif with subcellular-targeting moieties (acridine orange for nuclear delivery, triphenylphosphonium for mitochondrial delivery) to deliver theranostic radiometals to prostate cancer cells. The work explores whether directing radioactivity to specific organelles can improve dual-target imaging and therapy approaches for prostate cancer.

papers.title: Flexible Receptor Docking Provides Structural Models for the Recognition of 2‑Amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide Derivatives by Lck via the CorrEA Method.
papers.abstract: Structural models of Lck bound to a chemically diverse series of 62 2-amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide (AHBA) inhibitors were built to examine how the conformational state of the ATP-binding site shapes the structure-based interpretation of their potency. Docking to the static Lck crystal structure (PDB entry 1QPC) generated plausible complexes for only 54 of the 62 compounds, and produced essentially no relationship between docking scores and experimental pIC50 values, indicating that a single receptor conformation cannot capture how this scaffold is recognized. Receptor flexibility w
papers.summary: The authors built structural models of the kinase Lck bound to 62 chemically diverse AHBA inhibitors and found that docking to a single static crystal structure failed to explain potency (no correlation between docking scores and experimental pIC50). Using their CorrEA flexible-receptor method, they show that accounting for multiple receptor conformations is needed to capture how this inhibitor scaffold is recognized.

papers.title: Comparative Computational Investigation of Protonated Methamphetamine Inclusion Complexes with β-Cyclodextrin, 4-Sulfocalix[4]arene, and Cucurbit[7]uril.
papers.abstract: The molecular recognition of protonated methamphetamine (METH) enantiomers by β-cyclodextrin (β-CD), 4-sulfocalix[4]arene (SC[4]), and cucurbit[7]uril (CB[7]) was investigated using a comparative computational approach. Molecular docking was employed to identify favorable inclusion geometries, followed by density functional theory (DFT) calculations using the B97-D3/def2-SVP level of theory with the SMD water solvation model. Natural bond orbital (NBO), molecular electrostatic potential (MEP), reduced density gradient (RDG), noncovalent interaction (NCI), and independent gradient model based o
papers.summary: This study uses molecular docking and DFT calculations to compare how three macrocyclic hosts (β-cyclodextrin, 4-sulfocalix[4]arene, and cucurbit[7]uril) bind protonated methamphetamine enantiomers. The authors characterize the inclusion geometries and noncovalent interactions (via NBO, MEP, RDG/NCI analysis) to assess which host provides the most favorable recognition. The work is a computational screening of host-guest chemistry relevant to sensing or sequestration of methamphetamine.

papers.title: Combined DPD and MD Simulations of Surfactant-Coal-Water Interactions in Coal-Water Slurry.
papers.abstract: To understand the aggregate morphology and the interaction mechanism of the coal-water slurry (CWS) system, combined dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation investigation were used at 298 K. DPD simulations were used to examine aggregate morphology and component density profiles, while MD simulations were used to calculate radial distribution functions (RDFs). As the coal content increased from 5% to 56%, the morphology changed from dispersed aggregates at coal contents of 20% or less to interconnected aggregates at coal contents of 33% or more. Density profi
papers.summary: This study combines dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate how surfactant, coal, and water interact in coal-water slurry systems at 298 K. The authors show that increasing coal content from 5% to 56% drives a transition from dispersed aggregates (≤20% coal) to interconnected aggregate networks (≥33% coal), with density profiles and radial distribution functions revealing the underlying structural and interaction details. The work provides a multiscale simulation framework for understanding slurry stability and aggregation behavior.

papers.title: Mining, Systematic Characterization, and Optimization of Key Elements for Marine-Derived GDP-L-Fucose Biosynthesis.
papers.abstract: GDP-L-fucose serves as a pivotal precursor for the synthesis of fucosylated human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs), exhibiting immense potential in infant nutrition, the development of anti-inflammatory pharmaceuticals, and clinical diagnostics. This study aimed to identify high-performance enzymatic components from marine sources to construct a green and efficient biosynthetic system. Based on thermodynamic analysis (ΔG'° ≈ -72.0 kJ/mol), seven core synthetic enzymes were identified from three marine bacterial strains. Bioinformatics analysis and molecular modeling (AlphaFold/Molecular Docking) s
papers.summary: This study mined marine bacterial genomes to identify seven core enzymes for GDP-L-fucose biosynthesis, then used bioinformatics, AlphaFold modeling, and molecular docking to characterize and optimize these enzymes. The goal is to build a green, efficient biosynthetic route to GDP-L-fucose, a precursor for fucosylated human milk oligosaccharides with applications in infant nutrition and pharmaceuticals.

papers.title: Specifics of Classical Molecular Dynamics Simulation of the Raman Spectrum of the CO2 Fermi Dyad.
papers.abstract: Classical molecular dynamics is widely used to interpret the Raman and CARS spectra of supercritical CO2. However, the published positions of the Fermi dyad can differ by tens of cm-1. We show that the main cause of this scatter is the state preparation rather than the force field. A global Nosé-Hoover thermostat leaves the vibrational subsystem 40 to 100 K below the target temperature for hundreds of picoseconds, which shifts the dyad splitting by up to 20 cm-1 and the NPT-ensemble density by 50 to 70%, whereas a per-atom Langevin thermostat eliminates both errors. With equilibrated vibration
papers.summary: This study shows that discrepancies in simulated Raman Fermi dyad positions for supercritical CO2 stem mainly from how the simulation is prepared rather than from the force field used. A global Nosé-Hoover thermostat leaves the vibrational subsystem 40-100 K below the target temperature for hundreds of picoseconds, shifting the dyad splitting by up to 20 cm-1 and the NPT density by 50-70%, while a per-atom Langevin thermostat eliminates both errors.

papers.title: Tannic Acid Inhibits CaMKII-β Kinase Activity In Vitro and Displays Preclinical Anti-Tumor Activity in Ovarian Cancer Models.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is characterized by delayed clinical diagnosis, intrinsic/acquired platinum chemoresistance, and a high postoperative recurrence rate, highlighting an unmet clinical need for new targeted therapeutic strategies. Herein, we integrated pan-cancer transcriptomic profiling, clinical tissue immunohistochemistry, siRNA-mediated gene silencing, co-immunoprecipitation, structure-based virtual ligand screening, in vitro kinase activity assays, cellular viability functional assays, and SK-OV-3 xenograft mouse models to preliminarily reveal that CaMKII-β may mediate OC progression and
papers.summary: This study identifies CaMKII-β as a potential driver of ovarian cancer progression using pan-cancer transcriptomics and clinical tissue analysis, then shows that tannic acid can inhibit its kinase activity in vitro. In cell and mouse xenograft models, tannic acid displayed anti-tumor activity, suggesting a possible repurposed therapeutic avenue for ovarian cancer.

papers.title: Lomerizine Suppresses JAK2/STAT3 Pathway Activation via CACNA1B in HNSCC.
papers.abstract: The JAK2/STAT3 pathway contributes to head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) progression. Using a STAT3 reporter assay, we screened a panel of 79 compounds and identified lomerizine, a calcium channel blocker approved in Japan for migraine prophylaxis, as an inhibitor of reporter activity. Lomerizine reduced JAK2 and STAT3 phosphorylation in CAL-27 cells and suppressed proliferation in the HNSCC cell models tested. Ferroptosis-associated readouts and EMT-marker changes were observed in CAL-27 HNSCC cells. In cisplatin-resistant CAL-27-DDP cells, combined lomerizine and cisplatin treatme
papers.summary: The authors screened 79 compounds in a STAT3 reporter assay and identified lomerizine, an approved calcium channel blocker, as an inhibitor of JAK2/STAT3 signaling in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) cells. Lomerizine reduced JAK2 and STAT3 phosphorylation, suppressed proliferation, and altered ferroptosis and EMT markers, and it enhanced cisplatin effects in cisplatin-resistant cells, with CACNA1B implicated as the mediating target. This suggests a potential repurposing opportunity for lomerizine in HNSCC, though the work is largely preclinical and cell-based.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Reveals Persistent Alternative Binding Conformations of a Donepezil-Melatonin Hybrid in Human Butyrylcholinesterase: Implications for Alzheimer's Disease Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder in which declining acetylcholinesterase activity increases the relative importance of butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) in cholinergic regulation. Compound 4u, a donepezil-melatonin hybrid, was previously reported to inhibit human BChE with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 56 nM. We investigated its BChE-bound dynamics using three independently propagated 200 ns molecular dynamics replicas and a 100 ns simulation of crystallographically bound tacrine, totaling 700 ns. Compound 4u remained within the binding gorge in a
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations (three 200 ns replicas plus a tacrine control) to examine how a donepezil-melatonin hybrid inhibitor (compound 4u) binds human butyrylcholinesterase. The hybrid remains in the binding gorge and adopts persistent alternative binding conformations, suggesting multiple stable binding modes relevant to its low-nanomolar potency. These findings inform structure-based design of dual-target Alzheimer's drugs.

papers.title: Secondary Metabolite Profiling, Anti-Mycobacterium tuberculosis Activity, Molecular Docking and Dynamics Studies of Carpobrotus edulis Leaf and Twig Extracts.
papers.abstract: Herein, we evaluated the antimycobacterial activity and cytotoxicity of Carpobrotus edulis (C. edulis) leaf and twig extracts, profiled their phytochemicals using LC-MS/MS, and investigated the predicted interactions of the putatively annotated metabolites towards the Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) InhA protein (PDB: 2NV6) using molecular docking. LC-MS/MS profiling and MS-DIAL spectral-library matching enabled the putative annotation of metabolites belonging to several chemical classes, including flavonoids, terpenoids, and nitrogen-containing compounds. The antimycobacterial activity of th
papers.summary: This study profiled the phytochemicals in leaf and twig extracts of the medicinal plant Carpobrotus edulis using LC-MS/MS, identifying flavonoids, terpenoids, and nitrogen-containing compounds. The extracts showed anti-tuberculosis activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and molecular docking plus dynamics simulations suggested that some annotated metabolites may interact with the Mtb InhA protein. The work combines metabolomics with computational modeling to explore plant-derived candidates for tuberculosis treatment.

papers.title: Cavity-Guided Chemiluminescent Probes for Drug-Metabolizing Enzymes: Rational Design , Activity Imaging, and Translational Applications.
papers.abstract: Drug-metabolizing enzymes (DMEs), which are crucial for xenobiotic biotransformation, profoundly influence therapeutic efficacy, drug safety, and physiological homeostasis. However, conventional analytical methods such as LC-MS/MS and fluorescence-based assays face limitations in background interference, spatiotemporal resolution, and in vivo imaging, while the structurally diverse catalytic cavities and overlapping substrate preferences of DMEs complicate isoform-specific activity assessment. In this context, chemiluminescence (CL) probes, particularly programmable Schaap-type 1,2-dioxetanes
papers.summary: This review discusses the rational design of cavity-guided chemiluminescent probes, particularly Schaap-type 1,2-dioxetanes, for imaging the activity of drug-metabolizing enzymes. It highlights how these probes overcome limitations of LC-MS/MS and fluorescence assays in background interference, spatiotemporal resolution, and in vivo imaging, while addressing the challenge of isoform-specific activity assessment given the structural diversity and overlapping substrate preferences of DMEs. The paper covers design principles, activity imaging applications, and translational potential.

papers.title: Identification and Fc-Formatting of Alpaca Single-Domain Antibodies Targeting the Nipah Virus Attachment Glycoprotein.
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a WHO priority pathogen with case-fatality rates of 40-75%, and no antiviral therapeutic is licensed for human use. The attachment glycoprotein (G) mediates receptor engagement and is a validated target for neutralizing antibodies. Here, we aimed to isolate alpaca-derived single-domain antibodies (VHHs) against the NiV G head domain. Two alpacas were immunized with a baculovirus-expressed, truncated NiV G ectodomain (residues 170-575); peripheral blood mononuclear cells from the higher-responding animal were used to build an immune phage display library of 3.2 × 108 transf
papers.summary: Researchers immunized alpacas with a truncated Nipah virus attachment glycoprotein (G) and built an immune phage display library to isolate single-domain antibodies (VHHs) targeting the G head domain. The work identifies candidate VHHs and formats them as Fc-fusion constructs, aiming to provide a starting point for antiviral therapeutics against this high-fatality WHO priority pathogen.

papers.title: Machine-Learning-Guided Identification of Potent Osimertinib Analogues Targeting the EGFR Triple Mutant.
papers.abstract: Background: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations, including exon 19 deletions and L858R, are major drivers of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although osimertinib is an established EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), the emergence of T790M and C797S mutations can reduce its effectiveness. This study aimed to identify and computationally prioritize osimertinib analogues with potential activity against the EGFR L858R/T790M/C797S triple mutant using an integrated machine-learning-assisted cheminformatics and structure-based approach. Methods: A library of 297,420 osime
papers.summary: This study uses a machine-learning-assisted cheminformatics and structure-based pipeline to screen a large library of osimertinib analogues for activity against the EGFR L858R/T790M/C797S triple mutant, which confers resistance to osimertinib. The work computationally prioritizes candidate analogues that may overcome this resistance mutation combination, though experimental validation is not reported in the abstract.

papers.title: Phytochemical Characterization, Electronic Reactivity and Anticancer Evaluation of Symphyotrichum novi-belgii.
papers.abstract: Background: Symphyotrichum novi-belgii (syn. Aster novi-belgii) belongs to the Asteraceae family and remains comparatively underexplored from a phytochemical and pharmacological perspective. Symphyotrichum novi-belgii remains poorly characterized in terms of organ-specific phytochemistry and anticancer relevance. Methods: In this study, methanolic extracts of the leaves, stems and roots of Symphyotrichum novi-belgii were characterized using FTIR and GC-MS. Selected phytoconstituents were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and molecular docking against HPV16 E6, while the effect
papers.summary: This study characterizes the phytochemical composition of leaf, stem, and root extracts from Symphyotrichum novi-belgii using FTIR and GC-MS, then applies DFT calculations and molecular docking of selected compounds against the HPV16 E6 oncoprotein. It provides an organ-specific chemical profile of an underexplored Asteraceae species and computationally predicts anticancer potential of its constituents.

papers.title: Morus Prenylflavonoids as Candidate NLRP3 Inflammasome Inhibitors from an AI-Guided Natural-Product Screen with a Quantified Applicability Domain.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The NLRP3 (NACHT, LRR and PYD domains-containing protein 3) inflammasome drives interleukin-1β maturation and pyroptosis in chronic inflammatory disease, and no direct inhibitor has been approved. Natural products are a plausible source of new chemical matter for this target, but such collections are too large to dock exhaustively, and the machine-learning rankings used to triage them are routinely acted on without stating the chemistry over which they hold. This study prioritises natural-product candidates for NLRP3 while quantifying that limit explicitly. Methods: In t
papers.summary: The authors built an AI-guided screening pipeline to prioritize natural-product compounds as potential NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors, focusing on Morus prenylflavonoids. A key methodological contribution is explicitly quantifying the applicability domain of their machine-learning model, i.e., the chemical space over which its rankings can be trusted, rather than applying predictions blindly to large natural-product libraries.

papers.title: Bioactive potential of Cynanchum acutum L. root extract revealed by phytochemical, biological, and molecular analyses.
papers.abstract: Cynanchum acutum L. is traditionally used as a medicinal plant, but its aqueous root extract, particularly from the Algerian Sahara, remains poorly investigated. This study integrated phytochemical profiling, in vitro antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and photoprotective assays, multivariate analysis, pharmacokinetic prediction, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to characterize its aqueous root extract and explore potential molecular contributors to the observed activities. The extract contained 49.35 ± 0.85 mg GAE/g E total phenolics and 14.91 ± 0.57 mg QE/g E
papers.summary: This study characterizes the aqueous root extract of Cynanchum acutum from the Algerian Sahara, reporting substantial phenolic content (49.35 mg GAE/g) and flavonoid content (14.91 mg QE/g). Using in vitro assays combined with multivariate analysis, pharmacokinetic prediction, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations, the authors explore the extract's antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and photoprotective activities and identify potential molecular contributors. The work is largely descriptive and preliminary, with computational predictions not yet validated experimentally.

papers.title: Scutellarin is associated with reduced Ischemia-related inflammation and changes in miR-124-5p, AKR1B1 and miR-155: a potential mechanistic model.
papers.abstract: This study investigated whether scutellarin can modulate inflammation-associated responses after cerebral ischemic injury in association with a potential miR-124-Akr1b1 regulatory relationship, together with parallel regulation of the pro-inflammatory miR-155.
papers.summary: This study proposes a mechanistic model in which scutellarin reduces ischemia-related inflammation by modulating the miR-124-5p/AKR1B1 axis while also suppressing pro-inflammatory miR-155. The findings are preliminary and based on association rather than definitive causal evidence, but suggest a potential multi-target anti-inflammatory mechanism for scutellarin in cerebral ischemia.

papers.title: A reproducibility-audited, gate-based framework for early translational pharmacology: native-scale evidence, identifiability, and a 12-domain reporting checklist.
papers.abstract: Early translational pharmacology often combines docking scores, machine-learning structure predictions, and physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulations as if they formed a single evidentiary scale. This can create precise-looking but uncalibrated biological and clinical claims.
papers.summary: This paper argues that early translational pharmacology often conflates docking scores, ML structure predictions, and PBPK simulations into a single apparent evidence scale, producing precise-looking but uncalibrated claims. The authors propose a gate-based framework with native-scale evidence, identifiability checks, and a 12-domain reporting checklist, backed by a reproducibility audit. It is a methodological and reporting-standards contribution rather than a new empirical finding.

papers.title: Puerarin alleviates cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury-induced oxidative stress via the Neurl1/JAG1/Notch1 signaling pathway.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CIRI) remains a major challenge in stroke therapy, with limited effective neuroprotective interventions. Puerarin (Pue), a major bioactive isoflavone from Pueraria lobata, exhibits promising neuroprotective effects, yet its precise molecular targets and mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates how puerarin, a natural isoflavone from kudzu, protects the brain against ischemia/reperfusion injury. The authors propose that puerarin acts through the Neurl1/JAG1/Notch1 signaling pathway to reduce oxidative stress, identifying a specific molecular mechanism for its neuroprotective effects.

papers.title: Bisphenol a is associated with ovarian cancer chemoresistance via ecmCAF-mediated stromal remodeling: an integrative multi-omics study.
papers.abstract: BPA is a ubiquitous endocrine disruptor linked to ovarian cancer, yet its effect on chemotherapy efficacy is unknown. CAFs drive drug resistance via microenvironment remodeling. We investigated whether BPA exposure is associated with chemoresistance via CAF-mediated stromal reprogramming.
papers.summary: This integrative multi-omics study investigates whether exposure to the endocrine disruptor bisphenol A (BPA) promotes chemotherapy resistance in ovarian cancer through cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) that remodel the tumor microenvironment. The authors link BPA exposure to ECM-related CAF activity and stromal reprogramming, suggesting an environmental exposure pathway to chemoresistance. Findings are preliminary and based on association, so causal and clinical implications remain to be established.

papers.title: Survival of the fittest tool: choosing between open and closed artificial intelligence in pharmaceutical science.
papers.abstract: Three years ago, this journal published the editorial Technological Darwinism, urging pharmaceutical scientists to adapt to artificial intelligence (AI) rather than resist it. Since then, the question has shifted from whether to use AI to which AI to use, under what circumstances, and with what evidence. This review addresses that question by mapping current AI tools across the five canonical stages of drug development, from discovery to post-market pharmacovigilance. It is a narrative review, not a systematic one, and it treats openness as a spectrum rather than a binary. It compares two broa
papers.journal: Journal of pharmacy & pharmaceutical sciences : a publication of the Canadian Society for Pharmaceutical Sciences, Societe canadienne des sciences pharmaceutiques
papers.summary: This narrative review maps current AI tools across the five canonical stages of drug development, from discovery through post-market pharmacovigilance, and compares open versus closed AI approaches. It argues that openness should be treated as a spectrum rather than a binary and frames the choice between open and closed AI as context-dependent, requiring evidence about which tool fits which circumstance.

papers.title: Identification of dihydrokaempferol from Platycladus orientalis leaves as a potential therapeutic candidate for androgenetic alopecia through modulation of the KIT-mediated mast cell axis.
papers.abstract: Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is the most common form of hair loss, characterized by progressive follicular miniaturization. Current therapies mainly target androgen signaling and show limited efficacy. Emerging evidence indicates that immune dysregulation contributes to AGA progression, but its therapeutic implications remain unclear. This study aimed to identify active compounds from Platycladus orientalis leaves and investigate their mechanisms in regulating AGA.
papers.summary: The study identifies dihydrokaempferol, a flavonoid from Platycladus orientalis leaves, as a potential treatment for androgenetic alopecia by modulating the KIT-mediated mast cell axis. This suggests that targeting immune dysregulation, rather than only androgen signaling, may offer a new therapeutic angle for hair loss.

papers.title: An integrated computational and experimental framework identifies apigenin as a potential therapeutic agent targeting EGFR/STAT3/MMP9 signaling in glioma.
papers.abstract: Glioma is the most common primary malignant tumor of the central nervous system and is characterized by aggressive progression, high recurrence rates, and limited therapeutic options. Apigenin, a naturally occurring flavonoid, exhibits promising anti-tumor properties; however, its molecular mechanisms in glioma remain insufficiently understood. To systematically identify the therapeutic targets and molecular mechanisms underlying apigenin-mediated anti-glioma activity through an integrated computational and experimental approach.
papers.summary: This study combines computational target prediction with experimental validation to identify apigenin, a natural flavonoid, as a potential anti-glioma agent acting through the EGFR/STAT3/MMP9 signaling axis. The integrated framework links network-based target identification to in vitro assays, suggesting a mechanistic rationale for apigenin's anti-tumor effects in glioma.

papers.title: Integrated Bioinformatics and Experimental Analyses Identify PSRC1 as a Prognostic Biomarker Associated with PI3K/AKT/mTOR Signaling in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: To investigate the expression, prognostic significance, and biological functions of proline- and serine-rich coiled-coil 1 (PSRC1) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and to assess its association with WYE-125132 sensitivity.
papers.summary: This study combines bioinformatics analysis of public HCC datasets with experimental validation to show that PSRC1 is overexpressed in hepatocellular carcinoma and predicts poor prognosis. Functional assays link PSRC1 to PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling and suggest it may modulate sensitivity to the mTOR inhibitor WYE-125132, nominating it as a candidate prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target.

papers.title: A hierarchical gating hypothesis for GABA-Mediated gut-liver communication: a mechanistic framework.
papers.abstract: γ  -Aminobutyric acid (GABA) can produce divergent outcomes in colitis and liver injury, but the conditions linking exposure to organ responses remain unresolved. We propose a hierarchical gating hypothesis in which compartment-specific GABA exposure is an upstream prerequisite. JAK3-associated immune status and CDK2-associated proliferative status are proposed as parallel effect modifiers, not a fixed linear signaling cascade. Their possible roles as direct intracellular GABA targets represent a separate, unverified mechanistic extension. GABA-producing probiotic strains are considered potent
papers.summary: This paper proposes a conceptual framework—the 'hierarchical gating hypothesis'—to explain why GABA produces divergent effects in colitis versus liver injury. The authors argue that compartment-specific GABA exposure is a prerequisite, with JAK3-associated immune status and CDK2-associated proliferative status acting as parallel effect modifiers rather than a fixed linear cascade. The framework is a hypothesis-generating synthesis, not an experimentally validated mechanism.

papers.title: GPCRVS in the detection of target-selective molecular scaffolds based on deep learning and gradient boosting.
papers.abstract: High drug selectivity minimizes unintended interactions that cause adverse effects, decreases drug potency, and are failure-prone factors in many clinical trials due to a poor balance between drug efficacy and toxicity. Sharing similar structural folds and modes of activation, G protein-coupled receptors (GPCR) may represent difficult drug targets in terms of optimization of pharmacodynamic profiles towards drug target selectivity. Here, we describe GPCRVS, a web service for GPCR virtual screening, designed to detect selective drug-like compounds. GPCRVS combines machine learning for ligand-ba
papers.summary: GPCRVS is a web service that combines deep learning and gradient boosting to virtually screen compounds for selective binding to G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), a challenging drug target family due to their structural similarity. The tool aims to help identify drug-like molecules that preferentially hit one GPCR over others, reducing off-target effects. It provides a practical resource for computational drug discovery focused on GPCR selectivity.

papers.title: Rational Design of Benzofuran-Linked Isatin Derivatives as MTDLs Targeting MAO-B and Cholinesterases: Synthesis, in silico Insights, and Neuroprotection Studies.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders are multifactorial diseases associated with oxid active stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neurotransmitter imbalance, leading to progressive neuronal loss. Since monoamine oxidase-B (MAO-B) contributes to dopamine metabolism and reactive oxygen species generation, it represents an attractive therapeutic target for anti-neurodegenerative drug discovery. This study aimed to develop novel benzofuran-isatin hybrids within a multitarget-directed ligand (MTDL) strategy to achieve selective MAO-B inhibition combined with cholinesterase inhibitory and neuroprotective a
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized a series of benzofuran-linked isatin hybrid molecules intended to act as multitarget-directed ligands for neurodegenerative disease, combining MAO-B inhibition with cholinesterase inhibition and neuroprotective activity. The work reports synthesis, in silico docking/binding analyses, and neuroprotection assays, supporting the hybrids as dual-target candidates. It is a medicinal-chemistry lead-optimization study rather than a biological or omics resource.
